title: Use fog and camera previews
summary: Author global map fog and use temporary camera image, light, FX, and sound previews.
outcome: Map fog is saved while temporary previews help judge the scene without changing it.

sections.title: Author global fog

steps.title: Open fog controls
steps.text: Choose the fog button above the camera and check Enable fog. Set Start, Half distance, Max opacity, and Fog color while watching the camera approximation.

steps.title: Commit valid values
steps.text: The editor applies valid fog changes to the map as you edit. Press Enter or leave a number field to finish that edit; finish color selection by releasing the pointer or leaving the picker. Disable fog to remove the authored global fog values.

steps.title: Resolve an error
steps.text: If the panel shows a field or source error, correct the value before building. If controls are out of sync with the current map, refresh the editor before trying again.

tips: The camera fog preview approximates the in-game result; Build .ff also checks pending fog values before opening its build window.

steps.title: Open Film preview
steps.text: Choose the film button above the camera. Adjust Brightness, Contrast, and Desaturation, then use Highlights and Shadows to tint bright and dark image regions.

steps.title: Return to neutral
steps.text: Choose Reset in Film preview to restore the default camera image. Film controls affect only the camera view; they are not saved in the map or baked into the build.

sections.title: Control other scene previews

steps.title: Review lights and FX
steps.text: Use Lights above the camera to toggle sunlight, point, and spot light preview. Use FX to show placed supported effects; pause or restart their preview with the transport buttons when available.

steps.title: Listen to placed sounds
steps.text: Use Sounds above the camera to hear nearby placed sounds as the camera moves. The preview uses camera distance and direction; supported loaded sounds play on macOS.

tips: The FX and sound toggles are preview controls and do not edit placed markers. The Lights toggle is unavailable in compiled BSP preview.
